question: A group of boys has an average weight of 42 kg. One boy weighing 48 kg leaves the group and another boy weighing 38 kg joins the group. If the average now becomes 41 kg, then how many boys are there in the group?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net change in total weight = New boy's weight − Old boy's weight = 38 − 48 = −10 kg

Change in average weight = New average − Old average = 41 − 42 = −1 kg

Total number of boys = Net change in total weight ÷ Change in average

⇒ Total boys = −10 ÷ −1 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10 boys.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial average weight of a group of boys = 42 kg

Weight of the boy who leaves = 48 kg

Weight of the boy who joins = 38 kg

New average weight of the group = 41 kg

 
 Initial Group: n boys × 42 kg
 
 

 

 Leaves: −48 kg
 
 

 

 Joins: +38 kg
 
 
 Final Group: n boys × 41 kg
 
 Net Change in Total Weight = 38 − 48 = −10 kg

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

**Calculations:**

Let the number of boys in the group be n.

⇒ Total initial weight of the group = 42 × n = 42n

When one boy weighing 48 kg leaves and another boy weighing 38 kg joins:

⇒ New total weight = 42n − 48 + 38 = 42n − 10

The new average weight of the n boys becomes 41 kg.

⇒ New total weight = 41 × n = 41n

Equating the two expressions for the new total weight:

⇒ 42n − 10 = 41n

⇒ 42n − 41n = 10

⇒ n = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10 boys.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Change in Averages

When an item is replaced, Number of Items = (Value of new item − Value of old item) ÷ (New Average − Old Average).

Weighted Average

If group A has n₁ items with average A₁ and group B has n₂ items with average A₂, then combined average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Impact of Addition/Subtraction

If a constant value 'k' is added to or subtracted from all observations, the new average also increases or decreases by 'k'.
